subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Dakar Rally
description: A fast breakdown of The Dakar Rally for builders.

hook.text: The Dakar Rally originally crossed the Sahara Desert from Paris to Dakar, Senegal—over 6,000 miles.

buildup.text: Cars, trucks, and motorcycles navigate sand dunes, rocky plateaus, and riverbeds for two weeks straight.

discovery.text: Navigation is half the battle—crews use GPS and roadbooks because there are no marked roads to follow.

twist.text: Security threats moved the race from Africa to South America in 2009, and then to Saudi Arabia in 2020.

climax.text: The Dakar has claimed over 70 lives, making it the deadliest ongoing motorsport event in the world.

punchline.text: The most dangerous race on Earth doesn't even have a fixed course.

quiz.question: Where is the Dakar Rally currently held?

details.summary: The Dakar Rally is the world's toughest off-road marathon, originally spanning from Paris to Dakar, Senegal, and now held in Saudi Arabia over two weeks of desert, dunes, and unforgiving terrain.
details.whyItMatters: The Dakar tests vehicles and human endurance beyond any other rally. Competitors navigate by roadbook through featureless desert, making it as much about survival as speed.
takeaways: Originally ran from Paris to Dakar from 1979 to 2007
Moved to South America in 2009 and then to Saudi Arabia in 2020
Cars, trucks, and motorcycles compete across two weeks of stages

faq.question: Why did the Dakar Rally leave Africa?
faq.answer: Security threats in Mauritania forced the 2008 race to be cancelled. The rally moved to South America for safety, then relocating to Saudi Arabia in 2020 for financial and logistical reasons.

faq.question: How do competitors navigate the Dakar?
faq.answer: Each morning, drivers receive a roadbook with course notes, compass bearings, and distances. Using GPS for timing only, they must navigate by these notes at speed through featureless terrain. Getting lost is common.
